findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed member of staff to not use barrier when turning off hand sink. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and employee rewashed hands. Ensure a barrier is used when handwashing to prevent any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed prep cooler to be cold holding at 56F. Discussed with PIC, prep cooler door was turned off. Facility went through a deep clean roughly 2 hours before inspection, prep cooler was accidentally unplugged during that time. Prep cooler was plugged in and tested at 41F.  Ensure any TCS item being cold held is kept at or below 41F.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed soda gun at the waiter station to be soiled with mold accumulation. Discussed with PIC, soda gun was cleaned and sanitized. Ensure staff is cleaning soda guns at a frequency that prevents mold accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed hollandaise sauce to be hot holding at 100F. Discussed with PIC, sauce was moved to stovetop and reheated to 165F. Ensure any TCS item being hot held is kept at or above 135F.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed an open gallon of milk to be kept past its date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, milk was discarded and education was provided on date marking. Ensure any TCS item is properly date marked and discarded after.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: Observed a package of lobster to be thawing in a container of water with no running water. Discussed with PIC, thawing education was provided and container was moved to sink under running water. Ensure facility is maintaining proper thawing practices.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed bar soda gun to be soiled with mold accumulation. Discussed with PIC, soda gun was cleaned and sanitized. Ensure staff is cleaning soda guns at a frequency that prevents mold accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: Observed no certified food manager to be present during inspection. Discussed with PIC, facility will look into getting multiple certified food managers. Ensure one certified food manager is present within facility during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use.
findings.comment: Observed an employees canned beverage to be on prep cooler. Discussed with PIC, drink was relocated and education was provided. Ensure personal drinks are kept in approved containers and kept away from exposed foods.
findings.citation_text: 2-401.11(B) Eating, Drinking, or Using TOBACCO PRODUCTS.(B) A FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from a closed BEVERAGE container if the container is handled to prevent contamination of: (1) The EMPLOYEE'S hands; (2) The container; and (3) Exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  

Reporting agreements were only available for three employees when asked for by the inspector. Blank copies were grabbed from the facility’s stores and signed by all employees during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that all needed paperwork is maintained at the facility at all times.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The soda gun in the server area is observed soiled around one of the nozzles heavily as well as around the edge where the nozzles locks into the gun. The PIC was shown and cleaned/sanitized the item during this inspection to correct the violation. Nightly soaking in soda water HELPS slow pathogenic growth, but does not stop it. Ensure that the soda nozzles are CLEANED regularly to ensure that pathogens do not accumulate.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

The walk in cooler is observed to be holding TCS foods with internal temperatures between 46F-51F. Numerous items in the cooler were probed including ham, cooked pasta, sauces and hard cheeses. Both the inspector’s and facility probes were within one degree of each other and consistently registered high. Ham, garlic oil, parsnip purée, rice and cooked pasta were discarded during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. Refer to line item #33 for the write up on the cooler.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-201.11: (A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below). 

Multiple containers of poisonous substance such as RAID and steel cleaners not intended for food contact are observed on a shelf over the “clean” side of the dish machine counter. A discussion took place with the PIC and the items were moved during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that any chemical that is not intended for food contact is stored below and/or away from both foods and food contact items.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures. 

The walk in cooler noted in line item #22 is not functioning correctly and will need repair or adjustment. A follow up is being set for 2 weeks to ensure it is brought back into compliance.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed. 

The container of tongs on the prep line is observed with a white object covered in oil, hair, crumbs and other debris. The bottom of this container also has detritus and is in need of cleaning. The location was discussed and the container and tongs moved to dish for cleaning to correct.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. 

Observed two containers of sauce to be dated at 11/30. Discussed with staff. Sauce was voluntarily discarded. Ensure staff routinely looks through coolers and discards sauces. Food prepped should be on a 7-day date marking system. COS.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

(REPEAT) Observed the following areas in need of cleaning (non-food contact surfaces):
1. The baffles of the hood system were slightly soiled with grease debris.
2. The vent of the ice machine in the back area (where gelato is stored) has a layer of dust.
3. The underneath of the dish machine area is soiled with food debris and general debris.

Discussed routine cleaning with PIC. Ensure staff is aware to clean the above mentioned area. Repeat violations since the 4/6/23 and 9/19/23 inspections (#1 and 2). Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris. 

(REPEAT) Observed the following physical facility repairs that need to be conducted:
1. The walk-in cooler walls need re-painted on the outside, side by the prep area with gelato, and interior of the door. Paint is coming away. Re-paint the cooler to make smooth and easily cleanable. 

Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure repairs by next routine inspection. Walls and doors should be smooth and easily cleanable. Repeat from last routine inspection on 9/19/23.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

Cooler was serviced per employees. Bacon aioli (2x) temperature (probed): 52F and 53F respectively. Cooler does not appear to be working. Replace or repair cooler. Inspector will follow-up on 9/25/23. Bacon aioli (2x), chimmichuru sauce (2x), and red sauce (2x) voluntarily discarded.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

Observed no certified food protection manager (CFPM) available at beginning of the inspection. Mid-inspection, one of the owner’s/CFPM’s, came to the facility. Ensure the facility has multiple CFPM’s available. Multiple CFPM’s float between the various restaurants that the owner’s have. Ensure the facility has designated staff that are CFPM’s. Ideally, the facility should have 2-3 CFPM’s. Discussed with PIC. Provided educational paperwork on where to obtain CFPM’s licenses. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed the ceiling directly above the main prep cooler across from the grill/cook line to have dust on the tiles, vents, and circular hanging utensil storage device. Ensure area above the prep line is cleaned - wash, rinse, sanitize. Maintain food-contact areas free of dust. Inspector will follow-up on 9/29/23.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

(REPEAT) Observed the bottom reach-in cooler near the hot holding steam table and the grill/cook line to be keeping an ambient temperature of ~54F. Items probed included aioli (53F) and chimmichurri sauce (52F). Aioli, chimmichurri sauce, liquid egg carton, and various dairy based sauces were voluntarily discarded. This cooler had the same issue at the last routine inspection on 4/6/23. Isaac’s was called to service the cooler and Inspector asked to have this done again. Do not use this cooler until serviced. Place a hanging thermometer within the cooler in order to be able to verify ambient air temperature. Cooler did not have hanging thermometer. Inspector will follow-up on 9/22/23.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

Observed multiple coolers to lack hanging thermometers. Most had thermometers, but 3-4 were missing from coolers. Ensure extra thermometers are available at the facility and all cold holding units contain them. Coolers should have thermometers to maintain ambient air temperature verification. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

Observed no active sani buckets at the start of the inspection. Inspector asked staff to make sani buckets. Staff was already prepping food when inspection started. Ensure sani buckets are made prior to food preparation. Maintain active chemical concentration of sani buckets by changing frequently. Facility is utilizing quat - 200 to 400 ppm. COS.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

(REPEAT) Observed the following areas in need of cleaning (non-food contact surfaces):
1. The baffles of the hood system were slightly soiled with grease debris.
2. The vent of the ice machine in the back area (where gelato is stored) has a layer of dust.

Discussed routine cleaning with PIC. Ensure staff is aware to clean the above mentioned areas. Repeat since the 4/6/23 inspection. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris. 

(REPEAT) Observed the following physical facility repairs that need to be conducted:
1. The dish machine area in front of the spray nozzle has black mold on the wall. Repeat since 4/6/23 inspection.
2. Dish machine needs caulking to the wall on the side with the spray nozzle (coming away and missing).
3. The walk-in cooler walls need re-painted on the outside, side by the prep area with gelato, and interior of the door. Paint is coming away. Re-paint the cooler to make smooth and easily cleanable.

Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure repairs before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above. 

Observed pasta sauce on the hot holding steam table with an internal probed temperature of 122F. Inspector asked chef to rapidly reheat the sauce over the stove top to 165F. Temperature of the hot holding steam table was increased. Ensure hot held food items are cooked or reheated to the appropriate temperatures and then placed on the steam table. Re-heating on the hot holding steam table will not suffice. Discussed with employee. COS.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Observed a bottom reach-in cooler next to the cook line to have a temperature of 53F per the thermometer in the cooler. Inspector’s infrared temperature gun registered at 52-54F throughout the cooler. Cooler was turned down and temperature controlled foods were re probed. Items remained at 53F-55F. Pasta sauce (dairy based), crema, cheeses, and cut micro greens were voluntarily discarded. PIC stated he would call Isaac’s to repair the cooler. Inspector instructed facility to periodically check cooler temperatures and keep time/temperature controlled foods out of this cooler. Inspector will follow-up on 4/10/23. PIC was instructed to call/text AS tomorrow if the cooler issues before resolved before the weekend. If not, do not place foods in cooler except for the balsamic vinegars that remained in the cooler.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. 

Observed 2-3 spray bottles of sanitizer throughout the kitchen to have appropriate amounts of quaternary ammonium; however, none of the spray bottles were labeled with a common name of the toxic substance. Inspector wrote, “sanitizer”, on all the bottles in black pen. Discussed with PIC. Ensure spray bottles are labeled with the common name of the cleaning substance. COS.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. 

Observed multiple in-use rags throughout the facility kitchen. Facility is utilizing spray bottles of quat and therefore, the rags are not being immersed in sanitizer solution between uses. Cease practice. Facility may use paper towels with the spray bottles of quat and/or sani buckets with in-use rags placed in the sanitizer when not being utilized. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed the following places in need of cleaning (non-food contact surfaces):
1. Baffles of the hood system were slightly soiled with grease debris.
2. Interior of the fryer and the interior fryer door are soiled with an accumulation of grease and debris.
3. The vent of the ice machine in the back area (where the gelato is stored) has dust. 

Discussed routine cleaning of the above areas. Ensure staff is aware to clean. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris. 

Observed the following physical facility repairs that need to be conducted:
1. Tiles are missing on the left side and front of the pizza oven in the kitchen. Replace tiles and re-caulk.
2. The mop sink has moldy caulk around the basin of the sink.
3. Dish machine area in front of the spray nozzle has moldy caulking and wall has black mold.
4. Hand sink in kitchen needs caulked, as well as the bar hand sink (coming away from sink and wall). 

Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure repairs before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Observed allergen training certification to be expired for CFPM’s. Discussed with PIC. Provided educational handout on how to re-take the course online. Ensure all certified food protection manager’s re-take the course and print certification for the facility. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. 

An employee was observed to wash hands, use their bare hand to turn off the faucet and then acquire a paper towel to dry their hands. Education took place and the PIC is instructed to review hand washing with employees as well as ensure that proper hand washing procedures are used at the facility.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  

The deflector in the ice machine has black slime/mold observed along the bottom right corner and around the cracks and screw locations at the top. PIC consulted and the items cleaned during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

Inspector observed several items in the walk in cooler with internal temperatures between 44F-51F. Items were scattered throughout the walk in and indicate that the cooler is not currently maintaining proper food temperatures. Thermometers in the cooler also indicated 48F-53F. TCS foods were discarded during the inspection. Items included chicken, ham, milk, mozzarella cheese, and burette cheese. Per the PIC, multiple items were received from the day’s truck approximately 1-1.5 hours prior to inspection. These items were moved to other coolers/freezers throughout the facility. The walk in will only be used for non-TCS foods until the cooler can be verified to maintain proper temperatures. Facility should contact the inspector (card left with PIC) when the walk in is repaired/ able to maintain safe food temperatures.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. 

Four metal pans are observed on the back of the prep cooler next to the grill/ flat top. These pans are being used to store cleaned/sanitized utensils and are observed soiled. Inspector discussed with the kitchen manager, and the pans/utensils were moved to dish for cleaning. This same situation was noted on the 6/23/21 inspection. PIC is instructed to ensure that utensils are maintained clean until use.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

The condenser in the walk in cooler is observed with regular drips coming out and being projected throughout the cooler by the fan. Foods are currently all covered or in containers so no concern of contamination currently, the the equipment needs repaired to remove the drip. This was noted as a food protection item on 11/18/21. At the time PIC indicated that repairs would take place. Repairs needed again.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur. 

1) An employee drink was observed in the prep area next tot eh ice machine without a lid/ straw. PIC consulted and the drink discarded to correct. PIC instructed to review drinking/ eating procedures and related potential hand washing situations with staff. 2) On arrival, inspector observed a backpack and clothing laying on the backside of the main meal prepping counter. PIC instructed to ensure that employee belongings are stored separately from food contact of food preparation areas. The bag and clothing were removed during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS. 

An employee meal was observed on a counter in the center of the kitchen. PIC was consulted and the meal moved to an area separate from food preparation to correct.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

An employee was observed to eat (in the dish area) and then move directly to handling cleaned dishes without hand washing. Education took place and the PIC is instructed to ensure that proper hand washing takes place in the facility.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  

A consistent drip is observed coming from the vent in the walk in cooler. The situation is already being taken care of for repair, but multiple foods are observed open in the cooler. The blowing of the fan is pushing drops out to land throughout an area that encompasses multiple open containers. PIC was consulted and lids/ coverings supplied to protect the foods.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The inside spout of the soda gun in the server area is observed with a thick accumulation of dark colored slime. The situation was brought to the attention of the PIC and the items cleaned/ sanitized to correct.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-501.110: (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions. 

A phone was observed stored on the wood counter in the section of the facility also containing the ice machine. The wooden counter is also used for food preparation at other times. No food prep observed at this location at this time. PIC was consulted, the phone removed and the surface sanitized to correct.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS. 

An employee was observed to open and drink from a bottle in the dish area. Employee then proceeded to handle cleaned dishes. Education took place with the PIC and they are instructed to ensure that employees drink from containers only when prevention of hand contamination can be ensured, or when preceding hand washing.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed. 

Three pans are observed on the back of the prep cooler storing utensil and visibly soiled in the bottom. Discussion took place with the PIC and the containers and utensils were moved to the dish area to correct.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.citation_text: 2-401.11  (C) Provide a lid and straw for beverage cups in the food prep area. Employee observed drinking from an uncovered cup in the pizza prep area and then going back to food preparation. Discussed with the PIC and instructed them to ensure that all employees use sealed containers with a straw. Cup was given a lid and straw during the inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114  (P) Quaternary ammonium sanitizer measured 0 ppm at three compartment sink in the bar. The procedure in place is to add the solution from the machine intended for sani buckets to the water in the sink. The solution coming out of the machine should already be at correct concentration for sanitizing food contact surfaces and should not be diluted.  Maintain concentration at 200 ppm to 400 ppm. The sink was remade during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animal foods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. The buckets of sanitizer in the facility are observed to be predominately to weak to effectively sanitize food contact surfaces. Investigating the situation revealed that the machine that the buckets are made from is producing solution to weak to be effective. MJ Kelner is being contacted to service the equipment.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text: 4-904.13  (C) Preset Tableware is not protected from contamination. The pre-set settings are set with the eating ends exposed. PIC is instructed to ensure that place settings are prepared in such a way as to protect the eating surfaces from contamination. Tableware that is preset shall be protected from contamination by being wrapped, covered or inverted.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text: 6-305.11  (C) Employee phones were observed in areas near food contact surfaces or exposed foods in: 1) measuring station next to the ice machine, 2) in the dish area over and next to cleaned/ sanitized dishes, 3) on the central counter were foods are prepared in the main kitchen area. A packet of cigarettes and keys were also observed in the area next to the ice machine. PIC is instructed to ensure that employee belongings are stored in areas separate from food prep and so that they do not potentially contaminate food or food contact surfaces.
